mcq.q: 9 years ago a father was four times as old as his son. 15 years from now he will be twice as old as the son. The son's present age is:
mcq.explain: Let the son be x and the father y today. Then y − 9 = 4(x − 9) and y + 15 = 2(x + 15), so y = 4x − 27 and y = 2x + 15. Equating, 2x = 42, so x = 21 and the father is 57. Check: 12 and 48 (four times); 36 and 72 (twice).
mcq.fast: Back-substitute: take the son's age from an option, find the father from the first statement (4 × (x − 9) + 9) and test the second.

mcq.q: 5 years ago a father was five times as old as his son. 5 years from now he will be three times as old as the son. The son's present age is:
mcq.explain: Let the son be x and the father y today. Then y − 5 = 5(x − 5) and y + 5 = 3(x + 5), so y = 5x − 20 and y = 3x + 10. Equating, 2x = 30, so x = 15 and the father is 55. Check: 10 and 50 (five times); 20 and 60 (three times).
mcq.fast: Back-substitute: take the son's age from an option, find the father from the first statement (5 × (x − 5) + 5) and test the second.

mcq.q: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 9. The number obtained by reversing the digits is 63 more than the original number. The number is:
mcq.explain: Let the tens digit be a and the units digit b, so the number is 10a + b. Then a + b = 9 and (10b + a) − (10a + b) = 63, i.e. 9(b − a) = 63, so b − a = 7. Solving, a = 1, b = 8, and the number is 18. The reversed number 81 is the trap.
mcq.fast: Reversal changes a number by 9 × (difference of digits): 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Two digits summing to 9 and differing by 7, smaller digit first.

mcq.q: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 12. The number obtained by reversing the digits is 36 more than the original number. The number is:
mcq.explain: Let the tens digit be a and the units digit b, so the number is 10a + b. Then a + b = 12 and (10b + a) − (10a + b) = 36, i.e. 9(b − a) = 36, so b − a = 4. Solving, a = 4, b = 8, and the number is 48. The reversed number 84 is the trap.
mcq.fast: Reversal changes a number by 9 × (difference of digits): 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Two digits summing to 12 and differing by 4, smaller digit first.

mcq.explain: Multiply both sides by the LCM 4: this removes the denominators. Expand carefully — the minus sign in front of the second fraction changes the sign of BOTH terms, giving −x + 7 in the numerator. Collect x terms on one side and solve to get x = 1. Check by putting x = 1 back: (5)/2 − (-6)/4 = 4.
mcq.fast: Plug each option into the left side; only x = 1 gives 4. Integer options make this faster than solving.

mcq.explain: Multiply both sides by the LCM 6: this removes the denominators. Expand carefully — the minus sign in front of the second fraction changes the sign of BOTH terms, giving −x + 1 in the numerator. Collect x terms on one side and solve to get x = 9. Check by putting x = 9 back: (15)/3 − (8)/2 = 1.
mcq.fast: Plug each option into the left side; only x = 9 gives 1. Integer options make this faster than solving.

mcq.q: Solve the simultaneous equations 4x − 2y = 2 and 3x − 2y = 3.
mcq.explain: Eliminate one unknown: multiply the equations so that the coefficients of x (or y) match, then subtract. The determinant 4×-2 − -2×3 = -2 is not zero, so there is exactly one solution: x = -1, y = -3. Always check in both equations: 4(-1) + -2(-3) = 2 and 3(-1) + -2(-3) = 3.
mcq.topic: Simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns
mcq.fast: Substitute each option pair into the first equation, then the second; usually only one pair passes the first.

mcq.q: Solve the simultaneous equations 5x − 3y = -14 and 4x + 3y = -22.
mcq.explain: Eliminate one unknown: multiply the equations so that the coefficients of x (or y) match, then subtract. The determinant 5×3 − -3×4 = 27 is not zero, so there is exactly one solution: x = -4, y = -2. Always check in both equations: 5(-4) + -3(-2) = -14 and 4(-4) + 3(-2) = -22.
mcq.topic: Simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns
mcq.fast: Substitute each option pair into the first equation, then the second; usually only one pair passes the first.

mcq.q: If 2x + 2y + z = 8, 3x + 3y − z = 2 and 3x + 2y + z = 10, then x =
mcq.explain: Eliminate one unknown from two different pairs of equations to get two equations in two unknowns, solve them, and back-substitute. The solution is x = 2, y = 0, z = 4, so x = 2. The other two values in the options are the remaining unknowns — read which variable is asked.
mcq.topic: Three linear equations in three unknowns
mcq.fast: Test option triples mentally: put x = 2, y = 0, z = 4 in all three equations. Cramer's rule on a calculator also works (D = -5).

mcq.q: If 3x + 3y − z = 1, 2x − y + 3z = 31 and 2x + 3y − z = -5, then z =
mcq.explain: Eliminate one unknown from two different pairs of equations to get two equations in two unknowns, solve them, and back-substitute. The solution is x = 6, y = -4, z = 5, so z = 5. The other two values in the options are the remaining unknowns — read which variable is asked.
mcq.topic: Three linear equations in three unknowns
mcq.fast: Test option triples mentally: put x = 6, y = -4, z = 5 in all three equations. Cramer's rule on a calculator also works (D = -8).

mcq.q: The quadratic equation whose roots are -3 and -1 is:
mcq.explain: An equation with roots α and β is x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0. Here α + β = -4 and αβ = 3, so the equation is x² + 4x + 3 = 0. The usual slip is the sign of the x-term: it is MINUS the sum of the roots.
mcq.topic: Quadratic equations — solving, sum and product of roots
mcq.fast: Put x = -3 into each option — only the right one gives 0 (then check x = -1).

mcq.q: The quadratic equation whose roots are 8 and -4 is:
mcq.explain: An equation with roots α and β is x² − (α + β)x + αβ = 0. Here α + β = 4 and αβ = -32, so the equation is x² − 4x − 32 = 0. The usual slip is the sign of the x-term: it is MINUS the sum of the roots.
mcq.topic: Quadratic equations — solving, sum and product of roots
mcq.fast: Put x = 8 into each option — only the right one gives 0 (then check x = -4).

mcq.q: If α and β are the roots of 3x² − 5x − 6 = 0, then 1/α + 1/β =
mcq.explain: For ax² + bx + c = 0, α + β = −b/a = 5/3 and αβ = c/a = -2. Write the expression in terms of these: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/αβ = -5/6. Watch the sign of α + β — it is −b/a, not b/a.
mcq.topic: Quadratic equations — solving, sum and product of roots
mcq.fast: Sum = 5/3, product = -2; plug into (α + β)/αβ. No need to find the roots.

mcq.q: If α and β are the roots of 5x² + 10x − 1 = 0, then 1/α + 1/β =
mcq.explain: For ax² + bx + c = 0, α + β = −b/a = -2 and αβ = c/a = -1/5. Write the expression in terms of these: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/αβ = 10. Watch the sign of α + β — it is −b/a, not b/a.
mcq.topic: Quadratic equations — solving, sum and product of roots
mcq.fast: Sum = -2, product = -1/5; plug into (α + β)/αβ. No need to find the roots.

mcq.q: If α and β are the roots of x² − 11x − 9 = 0, then α/β + β/α =
mcq.explain: For ax² + bx + c = 0, α + β = −b/a = 11 and αβ = c/a = -9. Write the expression in terms of these: α/β + β/α = (α² + β²)/αβ = [(α + β)² − 2αβ]/αβ = -139/9. Watch the sign of α + β — it is −b/a, not b/a.
mcq.topic: Quadratic equations — solving, sum and product of roots
mcq.fast: Sum = 11, product = -9; plug into (α² + β²)/αβ = [(α + β)² − 2αβ]/αβ. No need to find the roots.

mcq.q: The roots of 5x² + 11x + 10 = 0 are:
mcq.explain: Find the discriminant D = b² − 4ac = (11)² − 4(5)(10) = -79. If D > 0 and a perfect square, the roots are real, rational and unequal; if D > 0 but not a perfect square, real and irrational; D = 0 gives equal roots; D < 0 gives imaginary roots. Here D = -79, so: imaginary (not real).
mcq.fast: Compute only b² − 4ac and read its sign; then check whether it is a perfect square.

mcq.q: The roots of 4x² − 6x + 2 = 0 are:
mcq.explain: Find the discriminant D = b² − 4ac = (-6)² − 4(4)(2) = 4. If D > 0 and a perfect square, the roots are real, rational and unequal; if D > 0 but not a perfect square, real and irrational; D = 0 gives equal roots; D < 0 gives imaginary roots. Here D = 4, so: real, rational and unequal.
mcq.fast: Compute only b² − 4ac and read its sign; then check whether it is a perfect square.

mcq.q: The roots of 3x² − 3x + 6 = 0 are:
mcq.explain: Find the discriminant D = b² − 4ac = (-3)² − 4(3)(6) = -63. If D > 0 and a perfect square, the roots are real, rational and unequal; if D > 0 but not a perfect square, real and irrational; D = 0 gives equal roots; D < 0 gives imaginary roots. Here D = -63, so: imaginary (not real).
mcq.fast: Compute only b² − 4ac and read its sign; then check whether it is a perfect square.

mcq.q: If 4x² − kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots and k > 0, then k =
mcq.explain: Equal roots need the discriminant to be zero: k² − 4 × 4 × 9 = 0, so k² = 144 and k = ±12. With k > 0, k = 12. Then the left side is a perfect square: (2x − 3)².
mcq.fast: Perfect-square pattern: k = 2 × √4 × √9 = 12.

mcq.q: If 4x² − kx + 36 = 0 has equal roots and k > 0, then k =
mcq.explain: Equal roots need the discriminant to be zero: k² − 4 × 4 × 36 = 0, so k² = 576 and k = ±24. With k > 0, k = 24. Then the left side is a perfect square: (2x − 6)².
mcq.fast: Perfect-square pattern: k = 2 × √4 × √36 = 24.

mcq.q: One root of x³ + 6x² + 5x − 12 = 0 is -4. The other two roots are:
mcq.explain: Divide by (x − -4) using synthetic division: the quotient is a quadratic, x² + 2x − 3. Its roots are 1 and -3. Check with the sum of all three roots: -4 + 1 + -3 = -6, which equals −(coefficient of x²) = -6.
mcq.fast: Sum of roots = -6 and product = 12: the other two must add to -2 and multiply to -3. Pick the matching option.

mcq.q: One root of x³ − 6x² − 25x + 150 = 0 is 5. The other two roots are:
mcq.explain: Divide by (x − 5) using synthetic division: the quotient is a quadratic, x² − x − 30. Its roots are 6 and -5. Check with the sum of all three roots: 5 + 6 + -5 = 6, which equals −(coefficient of x²) = 6.
mcq.fast: Sum of roots = 6 and product = -150: the other two must add to 1 and multiply to -30. Pick the matching option.

mcq.q: If x = 3 is a root of x³ − x² + ax − 3 = 0, then a =
mcq.explain: A root satisfies the equation. Put x = 3: (3)³ + (-1)(3)² + a(3) + (-3) = 0, i.e. 15 + 3a = 0. So a = -5. Errors usually come from squaring or cubing a negative root with the wrong sign.
mcq.fast: Substitute x = 3 once and solve the one-line equation for a.

mcq.q: If x = 2 is a root of x³ + 5x² + ax + 22 = 0, then a =
mcq.explain: A root satisfies the equation. Put x = 2: (2)³ + (5)(2)² + a(2) + (22) = 0, i.e. 50 + 2a = 0. So a = -25. Errors usually come from squaring or cubing a negative root with the wrong sign.
mcq.fast: Substitute x = 2 once and solve the one-line equation for a.

mcq.q: If α, β, γ are the roots of 2x³ − 14x² + 28x − 16 = 0, then α + β + γ =
mcq.explain: For ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0: α + β + γ = −b/a, αβ + βγ + γα = c/a and αβγ = −d/a. Here a = 2, b = -14, c = 28, d = -16, so α + β + γ = 7. The signs alternate: minus, plus, minus.
mcq.fast: Vieta with alternating signs: −b/a, +c/a, −d/a.

mcq.q: If α, β, γ are the roots of 2x³ − 8x² − 18x + 72 = 0, then αβ + βγ + γα =
mcq.explain: For ax³ + bx² + cx + d = 0: α + β + γ = −b/a, αβ + βγ + γα = c/a and αβγ = −d/a. Here a = 2, b = -8, c = -18, d = 72, so αβ + βγ + γα = -9. The signs alternate: minus, plus, minus.
mcq.fast: Vieta with alternating signs: −b/a, +c/a, −d/a.

mcq.q: The length of a rectangular plot is 3 m more than its breadth and its area is 598 sq m. The breadth is:
mcq.explain: Let breadth = x m; length = x + 3. Then x(x + 3) = 598, i.e. x² + 3x − 598 = 0, which factorises as (x − 23)(x + 26) = 0. A length cannot be negative, so x = 23 m and the length is 26 m.
mcq.topic: Equations reducible to quadratics and word problems
mcq.fast: Find two numbers 3 apart whose product is 598: test the options (23 × 26 = 598).

mcq.q: The length of a rectangular plot is 11 m more than its breadth and its area is 1,692 sq m. The breadth is:
mcq.explain: Let breadth = x m; length = x + 11. Then x(x + 11) = 1692, i.e. x² + 11x − 1692 = 0, which factorises as (x − 36)(x + 47) = 0. A length cannot be negative, so x = 36 m and the length is 47 m.
mcq.topic: Equations reducible to quadratics and word problems
mcq.fast: Find two numbers 11 apart whose product is 1,692: test the options (36 × 47 = 1692).

mcq.q: ₹1,320 is shared equally among some students. If there were 3 more students, each would get ₹22 less. The number of students is:
mcq.explain: Let there be x students. Then 1,320/x − 1,320/(x + 3) = 22. Simplifying, 1,320 × 3 = 22 × x(x + 3), i.e. x² + 3x − 180 = 0, so x = 12 (the negative root is rejected). Check: ₹110 each now, ₹88 each with 15 students.
mcq.topic: Equations reducible to quadratics and word problems
mcq.fast: Test options: ₹1,320 ÷ x − ₹1,320 ÷ (x + 3) must equal ₹22.

mcq.q: ₹240 is shared equally among some students. If there were 4 more students, each would get ₹5 less. The number of students is:
mcq.explain: Let there be x students. Then 240/x − 240/(x + 4) = 5. Simplifying, 240 × 4 = 5 × x(x + 4), i.e. x² + 4x − 192 = 0, so x = 12 (the negative root is rejected). Check: ₹20 each now, ₹15 each with 16 students.
mcq.topic: Equations reducible to quadratics and word problems
mcq.fast: Test options: ₹240 ÷ x − ₹240 ÷ (x + 4) must equal ₹5.

mcq.explain: Put y = 2^x. The equation becomes y² − 18y + 32 = 0, i.e. (y − 2)(y − 16) = 0, so y = 2 or 16. Then 2^x = 2 gives x = 1 and 2^x = 16 gives x = 4. The trap is stopping at the y-values 2 and 16.
mcq.topic: Equations reducible to quadratics and word problems
mcq.fast: Substitute x from each option: 2^(2x) − 18·2^x + 32 must be 0 for both values.

mcq.explain: Put y = 3^x. The equation becomes y² − 90y + 729 = 0, i.e. (y − 9)(y − 81) = 0, so y = 9 or 81. Then 3^x = 9 gives x = 2 and 3^x = 81 gives x = 4. The trap is stopping at the y-values 9 and 81.
mcq.topic: Equations reducible to quadratics and word problems
mcq.fast: Substitute x from each option: 3^(2x) − 90·3^x + 729 must be 0 for both values.
